definitionBean.title: Sector
definitionBean.definition: The region bounded by two radii drawn from the center of a circle and the arc between them is called a sector.
definitionBean.explanation: Area of the sector = (θ / 360°) × πr², and Length of the arc = (θ / 360°) × 2πr, where θ is the central angle and r is the radius.

definitionBean.title: Segment
definitionBean.definition: The region bounded by a chord of a circle and its corresponding arc is called a segment.
definitionBean.explanation: Area of the minor segment = Area of the sector - Area of the corresponding triangle. Area of the major segment = Area of the whole circle - Area of the minor segment.
importantPoints: Minor segment area = Area of sector - Area of triangle
Major segment area = Area of circle - Area of minor segment
A chord divides a circle into two segments

parts.statement: Find the area of a sector of a circle with radius 14 cm and central angle 90°. (Take π = 22/7.)
parts.explanation:
Given:
Radius (r) = 14 cm
Central angle (θ) = 90°

Area of sector = (θ / 360°) × πr²
= (90° / 360°) × (22/7) × 14²
= (1/4) × (22/7) × 196
= 154 cm²

Therefore, the area of the sector is 154 cm².

parts.statement: Find the area of a semicircle whose diameter is 28 cm. (Take π = 22/7.)
parts.explanation:
Given:
Diameter = 28 cm
Radius (r) = 28/2 = 14 cm

Area of semicircle = (1/2) × πr²
= (1/2) × (22/7) × 14²
= (1/2) × 22 × 28
= 308 cm²

Therefore, the area of the semicircle is 308 cm².

parts.statement: Find the area of the minor sector of a circle of radius 21 cm subtending an angle of 120° at the centre. (Take π = 22/7.)
parts.explanation:
Given:
Radius (r) = 21 cm
Central angle (θ) = 120°

Area of sector = (θ / 360°) × πr²
= (120° / 360°) × (22/7) × 21²
= (1/3) × (22/7) × 441
= (1/3) × 1386
= 462 cm²

Therefore, the area of the sector is 462 cm².

parts.statement: A wheel has a radius of 14 cm. Find the area swept by a spoke when it moves through an angle of 45°. (Take π = 22/7.)
parts.explanation:
Given:
Radius (r) = 14 cm
Angle swept (θ) = 45°

Area swept = Area of sector
= (θ / 360°) × πr²
= (45° / 360°) × (22/7) × 14²
= (1/8) × (22/7) × 196
= 77 cm²

Therefore, the area swept by the spoke is 77 cm².

parts.statement: Find the area of the ring formed between two concentric circles of radii 14 cm and 7 cm. (Take π = 22/7.)
parts.explanation:
Given:
Outer radius (R) = 14 cm
Inner radius (r) = 7 cm

Area of ring = π(R² − r²)
= (22/7)(14² − 7²)
= (22/7)(196 − 49)
= (22/7) × 147
= 462 cm²

Therefore, the area of the ring is 462 cm².

parts.statement: The radii of two concentric circles are 10 cm and 6 cm. Find the area of the region between them. (Take π = 3.14.)
parts.explanation:
Given:
Outer radius (R) = 10 cm
Inner radius (r) = 6 cm

Area of the region between the circles = π(R² − r²)
= 3.14(10² − 6²)
= 3.14(100 − 36)
= 3.14 × 64
= 200.96 cm²

Therefore, the required area is 200.96 cm².

parts.statement: A chord of a circle of radius 14 cm subtends an angle of 90° at the centre. Find the area of the minor segment formed by the chord. (Take π = 22/7.)
parts.explanation:
Given:
Radius (r) = 14 cm
Central angle (θ) = 90°

Area of minor segment = Area of sector − Area of triangle

Area of sector = (90° / 360°) × (22/7) × 14²
= 154 cm²

The triangle formed by the two radii is a right triangle with equal sides 14 cm.
Area of triangle = (1/2) × 14 × 14 = 98 cm²

Therefore,
Area of minor segment = 154 − 98
= 56 cm².

parts.statement: A chord of a circle of radius 7 cm subtends an angle of 60° at the centre. Find the area of the minor segment. (Take π = 22/7 and √3 = 1.73.)
parts.explanation:
Given:
Radius (r) = 7 cm
Central angle (θ) = 60°

Area of sector = (60° / 360°) × (22/7) × 7²
= 77/3 cm²
≈ 25.67 cm²

The triangle formed by the two radii is equilateral because the included angle is 60°.
Area of triangle = (√3/4) × 7²
= (1.73/4) × 49
≈ 21.15 cm²

Area of minor segment = Area of sector − Area of triangle
≈ 25.67 − 21.15
≈ 4.52 cm².

Therefore, the area of the minor segment is approximately 4.52 cm².

parts.statement: A circular garden has radius 21 m. A path in the form of a sector of angle 60° is made inside the garden. Find the area of the path. (Take π = 22/7.)
parts.explanation:
Given:
Radius (r) = 21 m
Angle of sector (θ) = 60°

Area of path = Area of sector
= (θ / 360°) × πr²
= (60° / 360°) × (22/7) × 21²
= (1/6) × (22/7) × 441
= 231 m²

Therefore, the area of the path is 231 m².

parts.statement: A circular sheet of radius 14 cm has a sector of angle 90° removed from it. Find the area of the remaining part of the sheet. (Take π = 22/7.)
parts.explanation:
Given:
Radius (r) = 14 cm

Area of complete circle = πr²
= (22/7) × 14²
= 616 cm²

Area of removed sector = (90° / 360°) × πr²
= (1/4) × 616
= 154 cm²

Area of remaining sheet = 616 − 154
= 462 cm²

Therefore, the area of the remaining part is 462 cm².

parts.statement: A quadrant of a circle has radius 14 cm. Find its perimeter and area. (Take π = 22/7.)
parts.explanation:
Given:
Radius (r) = 14 cm

Perimeter of quadrant = 2r + (1/4) × circumference
= 2(14) + (1/4) × 2πr
= 28 + (1/4) × 2 × (22/7) × 14
= 28 + 22
= 50 cm

Area of quadrant = (1/4) × πr²
= (1/4) × (22/7) × 14²
= 154 cm²

Therefore, the perimeter is 50 cm and the area is 154 cm².

parts.statement: A circular field has a radius of 35 m. Find the length of the arc corresponding to an angle of 72° at the centre. (Take π = 22/7.)
parts.explanation:
Given:
Radius (r) = 35 m
Central angle (θ) = 72°

Length of arc = (θ / 360°) × 2πr
= (72° / 360°) × 2 × (22/7) × 35
= (1/5) × 220
= 44 m

Therefore, the length of the arc is 44 m.

parts.statement: A chord of a circle of radius 14 cm subtends an angle of 60° at the centre. Find the area of the minor segment. (Take π = 22/7 and √3 = 1.7.)
parts.explanation:
Given:
Radius (r) = 14 cm
Central angle (θ) = 60°

Area of minor segment = Area of sector − Area of triangle.

Area of sector = (60° / 360°) × πr²
= (1/6) × (22/7) × 14²
= 308/3 cm²
≈ 102.67 cm²

Since the angle is 60°, the triangle formed by the two radii is equilateral.

Area of triangle = (√3/4) × 14²
= (1.7/4) × 196
= 83.3 cm²

Area of minor segment = 102.67 − 83.3
≈ 19.37 cm².

Therefore, the area of the minor segment is approximately 19.37 cm².

parts.statement: A chord of a circle of radius 7 cm subtends an angle of 90° at the centre. Find the area of the minor segment. (Take π = 22/7.)
parts.explanation:
Given:
Radius (r) = 7 cm
Central angle (θ) = 90°

Area of minor segment = Area of sector − Area of triangle.

Area of sector = (90° / 360°) × πr²
= (1/4) × (22/7) × 49
= 77/2 cm²
= 38.5 cm²

The triangle formed by the two radii is a right-angled triangle.

Area of triangle = (1/2) × 7 × 7
= 24.5 cm²

Area of minor segment = 38.5 − 24.5
= 14 cm².

Therefore, the area of the minor segment is 14 cm².

parts.statement: A chord of a circle of radius 21 cm subtends an angle of 120° at the centre. Find the area of the minor segment. (Take π = 22/7 and √3 = 1.7.)
parts.explanation:
Given:
Radius (r) = 21 cm
Central angle (θ) = 120°

Area of minor segment = Area of sector − Area of triangle.

Area of sector = (120° / 360°) × πr²
= (1/3) × (22/7) × 21²
= 462 cm²

The two radii and the chord form a triangle with included angle 120°.

Area of triangle = (1/2)r² sin 120°
= (1/2) × 21² × (√3/2)
= (441√3)/4

Using √3 = 1.7:
Area of triangle = (441 × 1.7)/4
= 187.425 cm²

Area of minor segment = 462 − 187.425
= 274.575 cm².

Therefore, the area of the minor segment is approximately 274.58 cm².

parts.statement: A chord of a circle of radius 14 cm subtends an angle of 90° at the centre. Find the area of the major segment. (Take π = 22/7.)
parts.explanation:
Given:
Radius (r) = 14 cm
Central angle (θ) = 90°

Area of the circle = πr²
= (22/7) × 14²
= 616 cm²

Area of minor segment = Area of sector − Area of triangle.

Area of sector = (90° / 360°) × 616
= 154 cm²

Area of triangle = (1/2) × 14 × 14
= 98 cm²

Area of minor segment = 154 − 98
= 56 cm²

Area of major segment = Area of circle − Area of minor segment
= 616 − 56
= 560 cm².

Therefore, the area of the major segment is 560 cm².

parts.statement: A chord of a circle of radius 7 cm subtends an angle of 120° at the centre. Find the area of the minor segment. (Take π = 22/7 and √3 = 1.7.)
parts.explanation:
Given:
Radius (r) = 7 cm
Central angle (θ) = 120°

Area of minor segment = Area of sector − Area of triangle.

Area of sector = (120° / 360°) × (22/7) × 7²
= 154/3 cm²
≈ 51.33 cm²

Area of triangle = (1/2)r² sin 120°
= (1/2) × 49 × (√3/2)
= 49√3/4

Using √3 = 1.7:
Area of triangle = (49 × 1.7)/4
= 20.825 cm²

Area of minor segment = 51.33 − 20.825
≈ 30.51 cm².

Therefore, the area of the minor segment is approximately 30.51 cm².

parts.statement: A chord of a circle of radius 14 cm subtends an angle of 60° at the centre. Find the area of the major segment. (Take π = 22/7 and √3 = 1.7.)
parts.explanation:
Given:
Radius (r) = 14 cm
Central angle (θ) = 60°

Area of circle = πr²
= (22/7) × 14²
= 616 cm²

Area of sector = (60° / 360°) × 616
= 616/6
≈ 102.67 cm²

Since the angle is 60°, the triangle formed by the two radii is equilateral.

Area of triangle = (√3/4) × 14²
= (1.7/4) × 196
= 83.3 cm²

Area of minor segment = 102.67 − 83.3
= 19.37 cm²

Area of major segment = 616 − 19.37
= 596.63 cm².

Therefore, the area of the major segment is approximately 596.63 cm².
